clue.text: A loveless sign? So be it!

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, so loveless means take that letter out

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader wonders whether a symbol lacking love is significant, then shrugs and accepts it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word closing a prayer is Hebrew for 'truly', said in assent as 'so be it'.

clue.text: Height of talent learner's shown for piano

indicators.note: one letter shown in place of another means swapping it in

parts.note: aptitude is a natural talent
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
L is the learner sign on British cars

explanation.surface: A tall student's gift is displayed at the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation above sea level or ground is a measure of height.

clue.text: Catch fish after getting new net

indicators.note: after puts the fishing word after the scrambled letters
new means the word is remade in a new letter order

parts.note: to angle is to fish with a rod

explanation.surface: An angler buys a new net before going fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To snare or ensnare something is to catch it, as in a net.

clue.text: Gives gears thrashing, like angry driver?

indicators.note: a thrashing beats something about, so the letters of the two words are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A furious motorist grinds through the gearbox, crunching every change.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile, combative behaviour is what an enraged motorist shows; the question mark flags an example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Shrub needing good 'ack?

parts.note: a hack is a horse; with the H dropped, as the apostrophe shows, horse becomes 'orse

explanation.surface: A bush needs a decent nag, spoken in a dropped-aitch accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Furze or whin, a prickly yellow-flowered bush of heathland.

clue.text: Taking it easy, is inside, not giving in

indicators.note: inside means the little word goes within the longer one

parts.note: resting means relaxing or taking it easy

explanation.surface: Someone lazing indoors refuses to budge.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding out against pressure is the opposite of surrendering.

clue.text: Wealthy firm

definitions.meaning: a person of means, well-off and prosperous

explanation.surface: A rich company.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both prosperous people and sturdy, solidly built things.

clue.text: Being victorious but not initially in baseball division

indicators.note: not initially means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: winning means being victorious

explanation.surface: A team is winning, though not in the opening part of a baseball game.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the nine periods of a baseball game, in which each side bats once.

clue.text: Branch of philosophy, hard one for unorthodox sect to grasp

indicators.note: to grasp means the scrambled letters hold the pair within them
unorthodox means unconventional, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tough philosophical school proves hard for a fringe group to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' turns SECT into ETCS, and 'to grasp' puts H and I in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral philosophy is the discipline studying right and wrong conduct.

clue.text: Volunteers doubling up for so long

indicators.note: doubling up asks for the abbreviation to be written out two times in a row

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Reservists pair off, and someone wonders how long that will last.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheery British farewell, like goodbye or 'so long'.

clue.text: Angry group of magistrates should be impartial

parts.note: cross means annoyed or angry
the bench is the body of magistrates or judges sitting in court

explanation.surface: Annoyed magistrates are reminded that they must stay neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: Independent peers in the House of Lords sit apart from the parties, so the word describes a neutral, non-party stance.

clue.text: Number competent that can be kept

parts.note: ten is a number
able means capable or competent

explanation.surface: A capable figure is described as worth holding on to.
explanation.definitionFit: A position or post that can be held or maintained is defensible in that sense.

clue.text: Wolves keeping supporters outside, walkers with their kit?

indicators.note: keeping means holding one thing within another
outside tells us the supporters word wraps around the wolves word

parts.note: backers are supporters
wolves hunt as a pack

explanation.surface: Wolverhampton Wanderers, the football club called Wolves, lock their fans out of the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Hikers carrying all their gear in rucksacks on their backs, often budget travellers.

clue.text: Wicked end to week, a kind you don't want to finish

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday, the day that ends the week

indicators.note: not wanting the finish means the last letter of the word for kind is dropped

parts.note: nice means kind or pleasant

explanation.surface: A wicked weekend ends with a kindness you would rather never stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish or diabolical evil is wickedness in its most extreme form.

clue.text: Enjoyment of naughty cat in act of destruction

indicators.note: in places the scrambled word inside the word for wiping out

parts.note: a deletion destroys or wipes out something written

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the three letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone takes pleasure in watching a mischievous cat wreck the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'act of destruction' reads as the cat's rampage, but it is wordplay; 'naughty' jumbles the pet and 'in' tucks it into the wiping-out word.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for delight or great pleasure, as in food served for your delight.

clue.text: Soldiers in a salute showing assent

indicators.note: in places the troops inside the welcome

parts.note: to greet someone is to salute them
men is a common word for soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: Troops give a salute to show they consent.
explanation.definitionFit: Concurrence or consent is assent, the state of being of one mind.

clue.text: Area 26 set up somewhere in Devon

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are read bottom to top, in reverse

parts.note: the answer to 26 across is the jazz word, four letters
a moor is an area of open upland

explanation.surface: A spot in Devon is fixed by an area reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns TRAD (the answer at 26) into DART.
explanation.definitionFit: A national park of granite tors and open moorland in the English county of Devon.

clue.text: Cleric is right, always having the last word?

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever
the end is the final word, the conclusion

explanation.surface: A priest is correct and insists on having the final say.
explanation.definitionFit: A title and term for a member of the clergy, a minister.

clue.text: Foreign father with broad smile had to travel around

parts.note: père is French for father
a grin is a broad smile
had, as in had a meal, means ate

explanation.surface: A grinning French dad has to go on a long journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander or journey from place to place, especially on foot, is a learned verb for roaming.

clue.text: Cricket side determined to get compensation

parts.note: the off side is the half of a cricket field facing the batsman
set means resolved or determined, as in set on winning

explanation.surface: A cricket team is resolved to get damages.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that balances or makes up for something else is a counterbalance.

clue.text: Part of Japan, a magnificent country

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A region of Japan is praised as a splendid nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central American nation, known for its canal.

clue.text: Working in cafe, Jane's ending as one who's found her man

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new arrangement
ending picks out the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: Jane, a waitress at a café, meets the man of her dreams there.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman engaged to be married has found the man she will wed.

clue.text: The old man, short character that is often very colourful

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, the old man

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: Dad, a brief figure, is said to be a colourful character.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's board holds paints of many hues, so it is typically bright with mixed colours.

clue.text: Letters at bottom of page about the French philosopher

indicators.note: about means the page letters go round the French article

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, is written at the foot of a page
la is French for the

explanation.surface: A note at the foot of a page discusses a French thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek thinker, pupil of Socrates, who wrote the Republic.

clue.text: Pet? It ceases to wander around in the morning

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the abbreviation
letters set to wander are moved into a fresh order

parts.note: am is the abbreviation for the morning hours

explanation.surface: A pet stops roaming about at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wander' jumbles IT CEASES, and 'around' puts that mix around AM.
explanation.definitionFit: This Thai breed of cat is an example of a household pet, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Spot troublesome animal in garden?

definitions.meaning: a small dark mark on the skin, a blemish
a burrowing creature that throws up hills of earth on lawns

explanation.surface: A gardener notices a pest digging up the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a skin blemish and the small tunnelling mammal gardeners hate.

clue.text: They initially organised squatting protest about nothing in passage

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word

parts.note: to run an event is to organise it, so ran means organised

indicators.note: about means the protest word goes round the next letter

parts.note: a sit-in is a protest in which people occupy a place
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Protesters set up a sit-in that achieved nothing in a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: Passage in the sense of a change or movement from one state to another.

clue.text: High-class violin not the first requirement for jazz

indicators.note: the first thing needed to spell the word is its opening letter, which is left out

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius, the finest kind of violin

explanation.surface: A fine violin is not essential for playing jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for traditional jazz, the New Orleans style revived in Britain in the 1950s.
